known_bad: two variants of the same census output, each of which must be red: (structure) one AAAI track's hit moved onto IL4 (another build's surface), one DR group spanning both builds, and one n_own set beyond nhit; (findable count) one TP with credited hits on 3 modules given a fourth, as a second hit on one module counted again would, judged by the identities; (tie break) one tied track (n_tp_top >= 2) given an owner, as index tie-breaking would
rule: on a fresh 4-event AAAI+IAAA census of the gate input run from this code root (angle cuts open, --calibrate): every exported hit lies on its build's active IT surfaces or the OT; every seed and follow surface is active in its build; every DR group lies inside one build; n_own <= nhit; own_tpidx = -1 iff n_own = 0 iff n_tp_top != 1 (no credited hit, or a tie: no owner, as CMSSW); identity of the counts with the reference: tracks, and the truth the census wires in (TPs in the census table, findable TPs (TF.findable: charged, credited hits on >= 4 modules, the efficiency denominator), tied tracks, and hits crediting their track's owner, which move if the stub credit of M.credited_tps stops reaching the census)
